To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
cross linking of polymers leads to a condensate phase which is a gel.
the infinite network is formed as a result of the condensation phenomenon.
the gelation of cross-linked polymers in solution is a phase transition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a variety of problems in statistical mechanics and its relation to polymer science.
the study of the structure of crosslinked polymers and the development of new techniques for their characterization.
the statistical mechanical properties of polymer solutions, melts, and gels.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the theory of the formation of the infinite polymer network from the solution is based upon the theory of the phase transition.

the formation of a gel from a solution of monomer molecules and cross linking agent molecules can be described by a theory which is essentially identical with the theory of the formation of a solid solution of a metal in a liquid metal.
the gelation process is a condensation phenomenon of the Debye Huckels type, and that the gelation temperature can be calculated from the Flory-Huggins theory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the formation of the infinite network is a thermodynamic process.
a polymer chain in a solution of bifuntional cross linking monomers can be described by a random walk model in a field of random obstacles.
a polymer chain in the melt is a random walk in the space of configurations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the condensation phenomenon is a general one, and that it is not specific to the particular form of the potential used here.
the condensation of a system with Debye-Huckel interactions is not a consequence of an infinite-range interaction.
the formation of an infinite network is a thermodynamic equilibrium process and that the gel point is a critical point of the system.
